closed.title: Searches log 'Search query:' and never log 'Search completed:' - establish whether the gap is client cancellation or a server-side block
closed.reason: CORRECTED 2026-09-20, SAME DAY: the delivered diagnosis first said PROCESS DEATH and that was WRONG. A live reproduction on a process that had answered a health_check seconds earlier showed the same signature with no death involved. THE CAUSE IS THE FIRST SEARCH IN A COLD PROCESS PERFORMING A HEAVYWEIGHT LAZY IMPORT INSIDE THE UNLOGGED WINDOW: py-spy located it exactly as search() -> _preprocess_text -> _ensure_nltk -> import nltk -> nltk.collocations -> scipy.stats -> scipy.linalg -> create_module, entered between the 'Search query:' and 'Search completed:' lines. The original argument - that a cancelled request would still log its completion because the worker thread survives cancellation - was sound about threads and wrong in its conclusion: a LIVE but BLOCKED thread never reaches the statement either, and the log now carries that exact test, a cancellation at 20:01:01 followed by no completion line. The task is still closed - a diagnosis was asked for and one was delivered, then corrected in place - and the follow-up is first-search-lazy-import-is-unbounded-and-unlogged. UNCOMMITTED and untracked: the rewritten DIAGNOSIS-SEARCH-HANGS.md carries both the wrong answer and the correction, deliberately.
